knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Microorganisms cannot be seen, so a visual check alone cannot confirm their removal.
The marker is a visible stand-in for soil. If it is gone after cleaning, the marked soil was removed. It does not show sterility.
The standard says routine sampling has considerable limits and is not routinely advised, though it can serve outbreak work and validation.
The a look is not enough section says verification gathers evidence that the method worked and that the schedule was followed.

practicalCriteria: Learner applies a fluorescent marker to a sample surface, cleans it, and checks it under UV, with the marker removal correctly reported
Learner writes a verification record for one surface with method, result, date and location, with all four fields complete
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation of the marker exercise
stopWorkCriteria: UV device is damaged or its instructions are unavailable
A marker or ATP product has no SDS
